subject: Discovery recap — Reliability & graceful degradation
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin Hart <kevin.hart@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-10T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap — Reliability & graceful degradation

Hi Kevin —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Per our conversation, wanted to capture the key takeaways and proposed next steps so we all have the same baseline.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Recent production incidents during peak holiday traffic (May and Aug 2026) causing client-facing timeouts and elevated error rates.
- No automated regional failover today; traffic all routes to us-east-1 which creates single-region risk.
- Lack of consistent SLOs across models/endpoints and limited visibility into per-route token latency/cost.
- Concerns about graceful degradation when upstream capacity is constrained (poor UX when timeouts happen).

Current stack (as you described it):
- In-house endpoints hosted on AWS (us-east-1).
- NGINX LB in front of autoscaling groups; Redis for session/KV caching.
- Some batching at the app layer; model workload spikes cause long queueing.

Incident history you highlighted:
- 2026-05-12: ~40m of elevated 5xxs during morning peak, root cause: autoscaler lag + model OOM on one pool.
- 2026-08-01: degraded throughput for ~25m after a failover attempt; traffic landed on a smaller pool in a different AZ and latency spiked.

Success criteria for a solution (your priorities):
1) Consistent end-user latency (p95 token latency target, and clear error budget).
2) Automated regional fallback to minimize single-region blast radius.
3) Deterministic behavior under overload (use of fallback models/approximate responses rather than hard errors).
4) Auditability/compliance: SOC2 and data residency assurances.

How Redwood can help (quick outline):
- Smart routing and multi-region model variants for automated regional fallback and reduced blast radius.
- Dedicated capacity and canary rollouts to avoid noisy autoscaler effects during peaks.
- Prefix/KV caching and continuous batching to reduce per-token latency and cost spikes.
- Graceful degradation policies: configurable fallback to smaller/quantized model variants, and automatic partial-response policies rather than 500s.
- Observability: per-route p50/p95/p99, token-level cost breakdown, and incident tracing for postmortems.

Attachments I’m including: SOC2-report-2025.pdf and a one-pager (redwood-sla-summary.pdf) that outlines our standard SLOs/SLAs and escalation flow.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with your infra/ML engineering (30-45m) — I suggested a few times below.
2) We’ll prepare an SLO appendix and a recommended fallback plan (models/regions) based on your traffic profile.
3) Provide references and a short runbook example for failover + canary strategy.

Do any of the above items need correction? If not, can we lock a time for the deep-dive next week (Tue/Wed preferred)?

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Kevin Hart <kevin.hart@acmeretail.com>

Cc: Aisha Rana <aisha.rana@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Reliability & graceful degradation

Ben —

This is great, thanks for the clear write-up. A few quick clarifications:
- The incident dates/impacts you listed match our internal postmortems.
- Data residency is a hard requirement for some of our customers (can't keep PII outside us regions).
- We would like an explicit example of the graceful degradation experience (e.g., what the user sees when we fall back to a lower-capacity model).

Procurement timeline: we’re aiming to include a vendor in our Q4 tech refresh (decision late Nov). We’ll need SOC2 evidence and a short runbook for our security review.

We can do a technical deep-dive Tue 2026-10-13 at 11:00am PT (our infra + ML eng). Can you confirm and send a meeting invite?

I’m attaching our incident log export for the past 12 months (acme_incidents.csv) — should help tune the fallback thresholds.

Kevin

Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Retail
kevin.hart@acmeretail.com | +1 (206) 555-0124

Ben
